name: Refuse a LinkedIn image or media address as a resume document
request: Refuse a LinkedIn image or media address as a resume document
checks: npm run check passed end to end: typecheck, build, 421/421 tests, validate (31 build files, 4 React entry points, service-worker imports)

rule 18 followed: the failing cases were added first and confirmed failing (profile-displayphoto asserted false) before the policy change; the four pre-existing accepted documents including the extensionless /dms/document/ABC123 were re-verified true afterwards

verified the built output carries both patterns (dist/src/applicants-core.js and dist/src/background.js each contain them); the source/dist hash differs only because dist is LF and the working tree is CRLF

NOT verified against live LinkedIn (rule 17): the hole is provable from the source, but whether it was firing on the user's account is a live-DOM question answered only by diagnostics.resume.foundWithoutOpening and the saved file's type
result: isResumeDocumentUrl accepted ANY licdn.com host on the host alone - no path, no extension - because an opaque /dms/document/<id> really is the file. But the pre-click sweep findResumeDocumentUrl(null) reads meta[content], [data-src] and [data-delayed-url] across the whole document including <head>, so an og:image or a profile portrait satisfied 'the address is already known': nothing was opened, and a JPEG was written to profile-vault-resumes/ under the applicant's name and reported downloaded. Nothing downstream caught it - the descriptor check only refuses JSON, the page fetch only refuses HTML, and the worker's host check passes media.licdn.com. Added NON_DOCUMENT_MEDIA_PATTERN covering /dms/image|video|audio/, profile-displayphoto, profile-originalphoto, company-logo and image/AV/asset extensions, consulted AFTER the document-extension accept so a genuine pdf or docx still wins however it is served, and mirrored it as RESUME_NON_DOCUMENT_PATTERN in the worker before anything is fetched. This protects the no-open path specifically, which is the one the user is asking to rely on more.
